title: 9E end-of-unit quiz
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Making materials (9E); conservation of energy
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 16 (9E end-of-unit quiz (portal quiz))
intro: Covers lessons 9 to 25 of Making materials (9E); conservation of energy. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: Why are ceramic tiles used around cookers?
options: They have a high melting point and are easy to clean
questions.a: B) They have a high melting point and are easy to clean. Ceramics resist heat and glazed tiles are waterproof and easy to clean.

questions.q: Why does a cross-linked polymer not melt when heated?
options: Bonds between chains stop them sliding apart
questions.a: B) Bonds between chains stop them sliding apart. Cross-links hold chains firmly, so they can't slide past each other as the material is heated.

questions.q: Why is poly(ethene) not biodegradable?
options: Microorganisms cannot break down its long chains
questions.a: B) Microorganisms cannot break down its long chains. Microorganisms lack enzymes to break the strong bonds in poly(ethene) chains.

questions.q: Which is the most sustainable choice for drinking water at school?
options: Buy a new plastic bottle daily and recycle it
questions.a: B) Use a refillable bottle. Reusing avoids making new bottles at all. Recycling is better than landfill but still uses energy.

questions.q: Which monomer makes poly(propene)?
questions.a: B) Propene. Polymers are named after their monomer. Propane has no double bond, so it can't polymerise this way.

questions.q: A tennis racket must be light, stiff and strong. The best material is…
questions.a: B) Carbon-fibre composite. Carbon-fibre composites are light, stiff and strong. Glass and ceramics are brittle; LDPE is too flexible.

questions.q: A coin scratches a material but a fingernail does not. Its Mohs hardness is between...
questions.a: B) 2.5 and 3.5. Harder than a fingernail (2.5) but softer than the coin (3.5).

questions.q: Why is firing a chemical change?
options: New bonds form and it cannot be reversed
questions.a: B) New bonds form and it cannot be reversed. Firing makes a new material that cannot be turned back into clay.

questions.q: Which result is an anomaly?
questions.a: C) 1100 g (bin bag). It is far from the other two bin bag results.

questions.q: Which is an energy store?
questions.a: C) Chemical. Chemical is a store; sound, light and electricity are ways of transferring energy.

questions.q: Speed doubles. Kinetic energy...
questions.a: C) is four times bigger. KE depends on v², and 2² = 4.

questions.q: When the band is released, energy is transferred from...
questions.a: B) elastic to kinetic. The stretched band's elastic store transfers energy to the car's kinetic store.

questions.q: 6000 J in 30 s. Power?
A 1.5 kW oven runs for 2 hours. Energy?
questions.a: B) 3 kWh. 1.5 kW × 2 h = 3 kWh.

questions.q: Which is a transfer, not a store?
questions.a: C) Heating. Heating is a way of transferring energy.

questions.q: Name the products of complete combustion of methane.
questions.a: Carbon dioxide and water

questions.q: Ceramics are...
questions.a: Hard but brittle

questions.q: Firing clay is a ... change.
questions.a: Chemical

questions.q: A polymer is made of many...
questions.a: Monomers

questions.q: Strongest bag in our test?
questions.a: Bag for life
